#
# Credential-literal rules, enforced by tools/ci/check-public-hygiene.sh as
# its second pass (the "Public-tree hygiene gate" CI job). They refuse
# secrets committed as literals. The patterns match SHAPES only; no real
# value appears here. This file is excluded from the scan, like
# hygiene-rules.txt.
#
# Line kinds (fields separated by TAB; blank lines and # lines are ignored):
#
#   rule         <flags> <name> <ERE> [options]
#                flags: E (required) and i (case-insensitive).
#                options (space separated):
#                  value-filter   the match ends in a quoted value; the
#                                 value is dropped when any "placeholder"
#                                 entry below matches it
#                  paths=a,b,c    only scan these git pathspec globs
#   placeholder-dq <ERE>
#                like placeholder, but applied to double-quoted values only
#                (variable references expand in double quotes; a
#                single-quoted '$Name' is a literal and is still reported)
#   placeholder  <ERE>
#                case-insensitive; a quoted value matching any entry is an
#                obvious placeholder, not a credential. Add entries here to
#                grow the list.
#   allow-path   <git pathspec glob>
#                a whole path is exempt from this pass. Use only for
#                fixtures that intentionally hold fake secrets, and put a
#                comment line above the entry saying why. The value must be
#                the exact path of one tracked file: no glob characters, no
#                directory, not empty, not "." or "..". The gate refuses
#                anything else and lists every active entry in its output.
#
# Per-line allowlist: a line containing the marker
#   hygiene-allow-credential
# (for example in a trailing comment) is exempt from this pass.
#
# Classes: securestring-literal, pscredential-literal, secret-assignment,
# private-key-header, token-shape.

# (a) ConvertTo-SecureString with a quoted literal and -AsPlainText, in any
# argument order or via the pipeline. A double-quoted string holding a
# variable reference ($...) is not a literal and passes.
rule	Ei	securestring-literal	ConvertTo-SecureString[^|#]*("[^"$]+"|'[^']+'|@"|@')[^|#]*-AsPlainText
rule	Ei	securestring-literal	ConvertTo-SecureString[^|#]*-AsPlainText[^|#]*("[^"$]+"|'[^']+'|@"|@')
rule	Ei	securestring-literal	("[^"$]+"|'[^']+')[[:space:]]*\|[[:space:]]*ConvertTo-SecureString[^|#]*-AsPlainText

# (b) PSCredential constructed with a quoted literal second argument, in the
# call form or via New-Object -ArgumentList (either order), and the
# -Password cmdlet parameter with a quoted literal.
rule	Ei	pscredential-literal	PSCredential[[:space:]]*\([^,)]*,[[:space:]]*("[^"$]+"|'[^']+')
rule	Ei	pscredential-literal	PSCredential[^|#]*-ArgumentList[^|#]*,[[:space:]]*("[^"$]+"|'[^']+')
rule	Ei	pscredential-literal	-ArgumentList[^|#]*,[[:space:]]*("[^"$]+"|'[^']+')[^|#]*PSCredential
rule	Ei	pscredential-literal	-Password[[:space:]:]+("[^"$]+"|'[^']+')	paths=*.ps1,*.psm1

# (c) a name ending in password, passwd, secret, token, api_key or apikey
# (so ADMIN_PASSWORD, $AdminPassword and GITHUB_TOKEN count; a name that
# merely contains the word, like password_file, does not) assigned a quoted
# literal of 8+ characters that is not a placeholder (see below).
rule	Ei	secret-assignment	[A-Za-z0-9_]*(password|passwd|secret|token|api_key|apikey)["']?[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*("[^"]{8,}"|'[^']{8,}')	value-filter paths=*.sh,*.bash,*.ps1,*.psm1,*.yml,*.yaml,*.py,*.json

# (d) private key headers.
rule	E	private-key-header	-----BEGIN (RSA |EC |OPENSSH |DSA |PGP |ENCRYPTED )?PRIVATE KEY( BLOCK)?-----

# (e) well-known token shapes.
rule	E	token-shape	gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}
rule	E	token-shape	AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}
rule	E	token-shape	xox[baprs]-
rule	E	token-shape	AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}
rule	E	token-shape	github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}

# Placeholder values (matched against the whole quoted value, case-insensitive).
# Entries are anchored on purpose: an unanchored word would exempt any
# credential that happens to contain it. The gate refuses empty entries and
# fails if the set matches the canary value Qw7rTz9pLm2x.
placeholder	^(changeme|example|placeholder|dummy|test|replace)([-_ .].*)?$
placeholder	^x{3,}$
placeholder	^your[-_].*$
placeholder	^secret$
placeholder	^<.*>$
placeholder	^%.*%$
placeholder	^\$\{\{.*\}\}$
placeholder-dq	^\$\{[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(:-[^}]*)?\}$
placeholder-dq	^\$env:[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$
placeholder-dq	^\$[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$

# Allowlisted paths.
# Throwaway TLS keys generated only for the unit tests of the HTTP client;
# they protect nothing.
allow-path	test/pagespeed/system/curl_test_certs.h
